plan: dispatch://LEGION-767/artifact/plan-md (version 1): nine ordered tasks, two code pushes (the self-check without the chmods first, red Worker Image run as the negative control; then the chmods, green), the rootfs proof with tar -xp and a positive control on the pre-fix image sha-40b71edb8b43, an in-package Summary test needing no production change, the legion-deploy production check reading the released digest's rootfs.

implement: legion-worker: the phase mechanics, the PR body and proof rules (references/pr-body.md), the push and handoff gate; the plan's two-push order and the rootfs surface depend on them
ce-simplify-code: the one simplify pass on the settled diff before the proof lines are final
test: legion-worker: references/pr-body.md says what the tester verifies and records; the tester re-runs the rootfs recipe with tar -xp (positive control on the pre-fix image, then the head's sha- tag) and reads lint/typecheck/test from CI
review: legion-worker: references/merge-gate.md and references/review-threads.md; the reviewer reads the diff beside the plan's quoted sentences, the :155 literal untouched, and both Worker Image runs (red then green) by id

findings.finding: The chmod bullet names only ssh-keysign while the self-check and the find -perm /6000 proof also refuse ssh-agent's setgid bit, so the fixed image as specified fails its own check.
findings.answer: Decision 1 / departure 1: the image also runs chmod g-s /usr/bin/ssh-agent (the deb's postinst sets it 2755, measured); group stays _ssh, no dpkg-statoverride; the comment and docs name both files.

findings.finding: The red step has no place to run as written and collides with 'one commit on top of main'; the image is built only by the Worker Image run on a PR head; whether Worker Image is required was unread.
findings.answer: Decision 4 / Tasks 6-7: the red step is the first push (self-check without the chmods), the fix the second; 'one commit' is the squash result. main's ruleset requires lint, typecheck, test, pr-title only (read with gh api), and the red lands during implementing. The self-check's command on the pre-fix rootfs is the cheap re-runnable control.

findings.finding: The rootfs stat proof is vacuous under the in-tree recipe: tar without -p strips set-id bits as uid 1000, so 755 prints on the unfixed image too.
findings.answer: Decision 5 / Task 5 / Task 8: extract with tar -xp, positive control on sha-40b71edb8b43 (4755/2755) before the head's image; the recipe doc gains the flag (departure 2).

findings.finding: Criterion 5 is not implementable as written without a daemon change: toolchain() returns a detail string, not a list, and the scope forbids daemon changes.
findings.answer: Decision 6 / Task 2: an in-package test calls toolchain() against the stubs, fails on !ok, recovers names with filepath.Base over the 'on PATH: ' detail and compares the exact Summary string; proven as a throwaway test against today's row; the :155 literal stays.

findings.finding: find / -xdev -perm /6000 names / as root but the proof runs on an unpacked rootfs in the pod.
findings.answer: Task 8: every proof command runs inside the recipe's unshare -r chroot, where / is the image and -xdev skips the mounted /proc and /dev.

findings.finding: 'The probe paragraph' is docs/kubernetes.md:94-96 inside the image bullet, which already says the builtin reaches only the bash tool; the edit must add something.
findings.answer: Task 4b: one sentence naming the two engines (the image's /usr/bin/jq; the harness's jaq builtin) and the rule to check an expression with the engine the script runs, citing the gotchas doc.

findings.finding: 'trixie's 1.7.1' is unsupported: the image prints jq-1.7 and the builtin's version is the harness's and drifts.
findings.answer: Decision 8: no version named for either jq.

findings.finding: 'add no egress … (curl, git, python3)': git's ssh transport becomes runnable, so the claim holds for reach, not for what the tools can do.
findings.answer: Decision 9 / Tasks 3c, 4a: the sentence is about reach (no host curl, wget, git, python3 and socat could not already reach); the Dockerfile comment says git's ssh transport is what becomes runnable while a pod's git speaks https through gh.

findings.finding: The withheld network row is a ruling, not enforcement; citing it as 'what a pod may reach' overstates it.
findings.answer: Decision 9: the texts call it Legion's ruling (dispatch://LEGION-5), a declaration the capability report renders, not a network control this repository ships.

findings.finding: The same NetworkPolicy wording survives at worker.Dockerfile:469 and docs/kubernetes.md:54 (ingress, socat).
findings.answer: Non-goals: left deliberately — conditionals about ingress, not the egress claim; recorded so the next reviewer does not re-file.

findings.finding: The self-check passes vacuously if its path is wrong; no evidence it can fail.
findings.answer: Task 3a: stat on both paths is the positive anchor (fails on a missing path, prints the modes), find names offenders, test -z fails; Task 6's red run and the pre-fix rootfs show it failing.

findings.finding: 'go test covers the two test changes' decides nothing about drift detection or the fold's guard.
findings.answer: Task 2 check: two mutation checks (drop jq from the Summary; add rg to onPath's names with a stub) each must fail; the :155 literal stays as the forgotten-name guard.

findings.finding: Which name survives the fold is unsaid and the current comment justifies the three cases.
findings.answer: Decision 7 / Task 1: python3 (pre-#1967 shape) with a comment naming the :155 guard and the lsp multi-absent case.

findings.finding: The two prose criteria have no check.
findings.answer: Tasks 3c, 4a, 4b quote the target sentences verbatim; the surfaces table says their acceptance is a human read against those quotes and grep -n NetworkPolicy as the control for criterion 2.

findings.finding: The production check names a route, not an observation; the daemon's probe reads no file modes.
findings.answer: Production check section: after the legion-deploy signal and the daemon's imageID read, pull the released digest with the recipe (tar -xp) and run stat/find/probe-image in the chroot; that read is the evidence.

findings.finding: Where the chmod goes is constrained to the root window before USER 1000:1000 and forces a full rebuild below it.
findings.answer: Decision 2: appended to the apt RUN at :475-479 after rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*; the cold Worker Image run is expected.

findings.finding: The guard is build-time only and the apt layer is cached, so it catches a rebuild of that layer, not a runtime drift.
findings.answer: Decision 3 / Task 3c: the comment says what the guard catches (a rebuild of the layer that brings a bit back).

specDepartures.spec: The Dockerfile's runtime stage drops the setuid bit from ssh-keysign (chmod u-s /usr/lib/openssh/ssh-keysign) right after installing openssh-client.
specDepartures.plan: Also chmod g-s /usr/bin/ssh-agent in the same RUN; ssh-agent's group stays _ssh; no dpkg-statoverride.
specDepartures.evidence: Trixie's openssh-client_10.0p1-7+deb13u4 postinst runs chgrp _ssh; chmod 2755 /usr/bin/ssh-agent (dpkg-deb -e, read by the planner); the spec's self-check refuses any set-id bit on /usr/bin/ssh-agent and its proof's find / -xdev -perm /6000 -path '*ssh*' must print nothing, so both bits must drop for the fixed image to pass its own check.

specDepartures.spec: Scope: the Dockerfile's runtime stage and its final self-check, docs/kubernetes.md's two passages, image_test.go and one new assertion beside it.
specDepartures.plan: Also a one-flag fix (tar -x → tar -xp, with one clause saying why) in docs/solutions/testing/prove-a-published-worker-image-from-a-pod-by-unpacking-its-rootfs-and-chrooting-under-unshare-LEGION-764.md at :32 and :86, the recipe the tester re-runs.
specDepartures.evidence: GNU tar 1.35 as uid 1000 strips setuid and setgid bits on extraction without -p (measured in this pod: 4755 extracts 755; with -p --no-same-owner it keeps 4755/2755), so under the recipe as written the spec's stat proof prints 755 on the unfixed image too.

outcome.scope: adds the one-flag tar -xp fix in the LEGION-764 rootfs recipe doc; the architect may drop it, and the plan's proof commands carry -p regardless
